newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Alcoa Australia to make up bauxite output.
newsitem.headline: Alcoa Australia to make up bauxite output.

text.p: Production of bauxite lost from the planned closure of the Jarrahdale bauxite mine will be made up by higher production from the nearby Huntly mine, the mines' operator Alcoa of Australia Ltd said on Thursday.

Alcoa is set to start winding down operations at the high-cost Jarrahdale mine in Western Australia, which produces 6.8 million tonnes of bauxite a year in about 18 months, an Alcoa spokesman told Reuters.
The lower-cost Huntly mine, which currently produces 11.9 million tonnes of bauxite a year will increase output to about 18 million tonnes to make up for the loss, the spokesman said.
The cost of the changeover will be about A$88 million, the spokesman said.
"Huntly will pick up all the lost output from Jarrahdale," the spokesman said.

"With old technology at Jarrahdale and longer and longer haul distances, the economics were not as attractive as they could be," the spokesman said. "We have no intention of going back there after rehabilitating the site."
The Huntly mine will eventually supply all the bauxite to Alcoa's 1.9 million-tonne-a year Kwinana alumina refinery and the 3.1 million-tonne-a-year Pinjarra alumina refinery, he said.
The changeover will have no affect on a third Alcoa bauxite mine at Willowvale, which feeds its Wagerup refinery, the spokseman said.
About 200 people were currently being employed at the Jarrahdale mine and the Huntley expansion would require at least an additional 100 employees, he said.
Generally, it take two tonnes of bauxite to make one tonne of alumina and two tonnes of alumina to make one tonne of aluminium.
Alcoa of Australia is 60 percent owned by Aluminum Co of America and 39.25 percent by WMC Ltd. The remaining interest is held by QBE Insurance Group Ltd.
